FD-1.baseline: the run raises (it splits a frame with numpy, which returns arrays, and then asks the array for .empty): a drop with several files per partition cannot be made
FD-1.shape: the partition is split into multi_file_chunks files of nearly equal size, each with a checksum in the manifest

FD-2.baseline: each source slot's late rows are written to <partition>_00900 immediately, so a later slot's late rows for the same partition replace the file: those rows are lost, and the result lists the replaced path twice
FD-2.shape: the late rows of every slot that land in one partition share that one 00900 file (oldest slot first); nothing is lost and each file is listed once
FD-2.what: late arrivals landing in the same partition

FD-3.baseline: a column named like a date (date, timestamp, created, updated) is the time column when pandas can parse its values: an integer column such as updated_count is read as nanoseconds since 1970, every row falls outside the date range and the drop silently writes nothing
FD-3.shape: only dates, timestamps and ISO-8601 text can be the time column; a table without one is dealt out round robin

FD-4.baseline: an unknown cadence is treated as daily (the manifest still says the unknown name), and an end date before the start date writes nothing without an error
FD-4.shape: both raise a ValueError that names the setting

FD-5.baseline: a timestamp is written to the millisecond (pandas to_json's default unit), so a value with microseconds or nanoseconds silently loses them: the JSON Lines file does not hold what the Parquet file of the same drop holds
FD-5.shape: the full precision of the column is written

HY-1.baseline: the run's id is written only into the _correlation_id column of the rows; every manifest and every event has a correlation id of its own, so the files and the events cannot be joined on what the documentation says they share
HY-1.shape: the run id is also the correlation_id of every manifest and the correlationid of every event (with the natural_keys strategy nothing is stamped, as before)
HY-1.what: the run id in manifests and events

HY-2.shape: raises a ValueError that names the table
HY-2.what: an unknown table name in stream_tables or batch_tables

SCD-1.baseline: the state is built from the table, not from the snapshot, so the first time a record changes its expired row has no valid_from (null) although the snapshot gave it one
SCD-1.shape: the expired row keeps the valid_from of the version it expires (the initial date, or the day the entity was inserted)

SCD-2.baseline: an insert copies the first entity's row as it is in the state; while that entity has never changed it has no version columns, so the insert has valid_from null, valid_to null and is_current null (not true)
SCD-2.shape: an insert has valid_from = the day, valid_to null and is_current true
SCD-2.what: version columns of an inserted entity

SCD-3.baseline: a delta's columns are the union of its rows' keys in order of first appearance: valid_to, is_current, _delta_type and valid_from come after the table's columns in an order that depends on the first row, and differs from the snapshot's
SCD-3.shape: every delta has the snapshot's columns in the snapshot's order, then _delta_type
SCD-3.what: column order of the delta files

SCD-4.baseline: pandas holds such a column as float, so a changed value is the product with the factor, unrounded: an id column ends with values such as 889.73
SCD-4.shape: an integer stays an integer: the product is rounded to the nearest integer (halves to even)
SCD-4.what: changing an integer column that has nulls

SCD-5.baseline: the first delta mixes text keys with the integer keys of the inserts, and the write fails with an Arrow conversion error after the snapshot is on disk
SCD-5.shape: the run raises a ValueError that names the key column, before anything is written
SCD-5.what: a business key that is not numeric

WF-1.baseline: an entity whose initial state has no way out has no events, and its summary row says it started and ended in the first initial state of the workflow, whichever state it was actually given
WF-1.shape: its summary row names the state it started in
WF-1.what: entities that never move (their initial state)

WF-2.baseline: a new random UUID for every event on every run: the same seed gives a different event_id column each time
WF-2.shape: a UUID derived from the seed (a stream of its own, so no other draw moves): the same seed gives the same ids (a determinism rule, not a defect)

SE-1.baseline: the setting is accepted and never read: a paced run with a burst window runs at the base rate throughout

SE-2.baseline: accepted and replaced by the console sink: the events go to standard output and nothing is sent anywhere

SE-3.baseline: a new random correlation_id for every event, so no two events of a run share one and nothing can be joined on it
SE-3.shape: one correlationid for the whole run (the hybrid simulator passes its own run id to its manifests and events)

SE-4.baseline: the replay buffer survives between calls: a second emit() can send again events of the first call that are not among its own events
SE-4.shape: the window starts empty at every call: a replay is only ever of this call's events
